The following Firefox/GreaseMonkey JS snippet is the only way I tolerate that "other" site and their backwards-ass algorithm that incessantly displays the same submissions over and over, wasting my time, as I paginate through the system. Basically, if I've already SEEN it, don't show it to me again.

Coming from a technical background, I understand this might be a PITA to implement server-side depending on the DB structure/inserts....but for what it's worth, I use the following to accomplish this on the client-side:

//Remove existing stored submissions
for(i=0;i<=window.sessionStorage.length;i++) {
 $(".submission[data-fullname='"+window.sessionStorage.key(i)+"']").remove();
}

//Store submissions
$.each($(".submission"),function() {
 window.sessionStorage.setItem($(this).attr("data-fullname"),true);
});

Hope this helps to some extent - it has so greatly improved my experience on both sites so far that I would love to see other people enjoy it as I do without needing browser plugins, code snippets, or what-have-you. And thanks for reading this - keep doing what you're doing, guys.
